gaps.finding: Link worldly-information safety for modal knowledge to assessment-sensitive retraction: explain how information used for safety at nearby worlds relates to a later assessment context and what licenses the retraction obligation. Mere conjunction, common symbols, or treating assessor information as worldly information does not establish this link.

evidence.finding: Retraction is motivated by no longer standing by an update; no fixed-use assessment rule is derived.
Assessor information rejects a modal-knowledge ascription and explicitly cites MacFarlane2014.
Knowledge combines truth, belief and worldly-information safety across nearby worlds. Safety is separately stated from truth at an information index.
Worldly information may be contextually selected; assessor credences are one possible probability interpretation, without deriving assessment-sensitive retraction.
Retraction fixes the earlier use context and changes the assessment context. Rejection permission differs from retraction obligation.
The retraction discussion applies to epistemic modals.

An asymmetric-loss explanation links retraction of knowledge ascriptions to estimates of epistemic qualities including safety/reliability, consistently with denying relativism. This is a rival behavioral bridge, not the requested worldly-information semantics.
Cites modal knowledge but leaves truth/correctness/agreement/retraction pragmatics for development, compatible with multiple approaches.
